engineers: The UCTE investigation found that coupling the Landesbergen busbars had the opposite effect to what the dispatchers expected: instead of falling by about 80 A, the current on Landesbergen-Wehrendorf rose by about 67 A (about 50 MW) and the line was tripped by the distance protection at Wehrendorf, starting a cascade that split the UCTE grid into three areas and cut supply to more than 15 million households. The grid had not been N-1 secure since Conneforde-Diele was switched off: an outage of Bechterdissen-Elsen or Elsen-Twistetal would have pushed the tie above the 2,100 A trip setting.
source: UCTE Final Report, System Disturbance on 4 November 2006 (30 January 2007), p.19 (coupling effect, +67 A), p.48 (N-1 violation), p.50-51 (Fig. 30/31), p.5 (impact)
